Real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 is estimated at 7.6%, higher than the 7.1% recorded in FY 2024-25, with nominal GDP growing at 8.6% in current price terms, driven by the twin engines of robust private consumption and sustained capital investment.

Outlook India's growth outlook remains strong, with real GDP projected in the range of 6.8%-7.2% in FY27, supported by resilient domestic demand, continued infrastructure spending, and stable macroeconomic fundamentals.
Growth & demand: Downside risks remain significant: under an adverse scenario with more persistent energy disruptions, global growth could slow further to 2.5% with inflation rising to 5.4%, while a severe scenario could bring growth close to 2.0% alongside headline inflation approaching 6%.

Growth remained broad-based, agriculture expanded by 3.1% on the back of above-normal monsoon and record crop production, industry grew at 6.2% led by double-digit manufacturing momentum, and the services sector expanded by 9.1%, remaining the largest contributor to GDP.

(Source: IBEF) The sector is expected to record revenue growth of 6-8% in FY26, driven by a gradual resurgence in urban demand and consistent rural consumption, translating to a volume increase of 4-6%.
Margins & costs: Increasing Material and Cost Volatility Fluctuations in crude oil prices and global supply chain disruptions continue to impact raw material costs, influencing margins and pricing strategies.
Inflation moderated sharply, with headline CPI averaging 1.7%, the lowest since the 2014-base series began, driven by food price disinflation and easing global commodity prices.

Raw Material Availability and Pricing Risk The Company remains exposed to fluctuations in the availability and pricing of polymer-based raw materials, driven by crude oil volatility, geopolitical developments and global supply-demand imbalances.
